speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These efforts were first initiated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) to deal with the issue of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) by MNEs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To ensure a wider international consensus, the discussions were subsequently broadened to include more than 130 jurisdictions through a platform called the Inclusive Framework on BEPS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore has been actively involved in these international discussions as part of the Inclusive Framework (IF).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The IF has been discussing two major tax changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The first proposal concerns the reallocation of taxing rights of the largest and most profitable MNEs from where they conduct their substantial activities to where their customers are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The second proposal is the introduction of an internationally agreed minimum corporate tax rate for large MNEs, wherever they operate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Pillar One was intended to adapt the international tax system to new business models where large businesses sell remotely to consumers in other jurisdictions, without physical presence.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under Pillar One, some part of the profits and hence, the taxes payable of large companies with overseas operations will be reallocated to where their customers are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To illustrate, assume a Pillar One MNE group in Singapore has a profitability of 15%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Pillar One will then reallocate a portion of the profits in excess of 10%, 5% in this case, from Singapore to be taxed in the market jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that hub economies with smaller markets like Singapore will stand to lose corporate income tax revenues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Pillar Two aims to put a floor on international corporate tax competition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Essentially, under this proposal, MNEs will be subject to the minimum effective tax rate of 15% at the MNE group level, in every jurisdiction they operate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Broadly speaking, this means that if an MNE group in Singapore is taxed at an effective rate of, say 10%, then its home jurisdiction will impose additional rules to require the group to pay an additional 5% in tax there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Pillar Two will therefore limit the effectiveness of tax incentives as a tool to encourage larger MNEs to invest in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked how many MNEs in Singapore currently pay less than the global minimum corporate tax rate of 15%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We expect that a majority of these MNE groups will have group effective tax rates below 15% in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is because our headline corporate tax rate is 17%, close to the proposed minimum effective tax rate of 15%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Furthermore, our tax system, like most others, provides for tax reliefs to encourage various meritorious activities like capital investment, R&D or charitable donations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And for a small number of companies, there are also tax incentives for their qualifying activities subject to economic commitments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: However, at this stage, it is still too early to work out the exact impact of the tax proposals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The final number of affected MNEs, as well as the extent of the impact, depends on the design of the specific rules which are still being actively discussed at the IF.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As some of the tax proposals can only be effected through a multilateral instrument, there will be a need for international consensus to be fully reached before the changes can be implemented.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, in response to the query from Ms Foo, we will only be able to determine with a high degree of confidence what the eventual impact on Singapore's fiscal position would be, once the IF has worked through and agreed on the detailed design elements of both Pillars.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The eventual impact will also depend on how companies and other governments respond to these international developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What we can say for certain is that when a consensus is fully reached, Singapore will adjust our corporate tax system as needed, in consultation with the industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Any adjustments to our tax system will be guided by three principles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, we will abide by internationally agreed standards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, we will seek to minimise the compliance burden for businesses.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ultimately, the best response to these tax changes is to continue to strengthen our overall competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the decades, Singapore has built a solid reputation and track record as an attractive place for business and substantial economic activity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While a conducive tax environment has been helpful in attracting investments, it is not the decisive factor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Having quality infrastructure, good connectivity, a skilled workforce, an open and business-friendly regime founded on the rule of law, are all far more important factors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must therefore double down on these competitive strengths.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, the Government has been investing and will continue to invest in enterprise capabilities, including innovation and digitalisation, and in the skills of our workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry will be elaborating further on how Singapore can continue to strengthen its position as a hub.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore has also separately provided a written answer to Ms Mariam Jaafar's question on Singapore's position as an international financial centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must continually work hard to strengthen our value proposition, build new advantages and seek new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This way, we can ensure Singapore's continued economic success and ultimately a good future for our people.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I understand a lot of details are not out yet but, I guess, with the announcement, there has been a lot of interest in the industry.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Whilst we expect the tax system to evolve, I would like to hear the Minister's thoughts on, for the Minister to speak a little bit more about what specific non-tax benefit could Singapore provide or enhance, in order to compensate for the loss of tax benefits, previously enjoyed by companies, so that there is some level of certainty when companies are planning.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I understand that financial services have been a carve-out from this global tax reform.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Could the Minister comment on how the financial sector is being impacted including family offices and variable capital companies (VCCs)?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And last but not least, on jurisdictions that have been tax havens, without the other non-tax benefits.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As for Pillar Two, as I have mentioned, it applies to the larger MNEs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, whether or not family offices and VCCs will qualify, will really depend on the facts of the case, and ultimately, what are the final criteria that are used for the definition of large MNEs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to monitor this closely.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as I said earlier, we will respond accordingly once the international rules are worked out and finalised.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Number two, we will continue to work hard at improving and enhancing our competitiveness in other areas, especially in terms of the non-tax factors that Ms Foo highlighted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, to Ms Foo's question, yes, this is work in progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have always been looking at how we can restructure, transform our economy, invest in enterprise capabilities, as well as the capabilities of our workforce.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will work even harder at that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our objective is to continue to remain attractive and competitive; attractive to substantial investments and substantial economic activities to be based here.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are not trying to get companies to register in Singapore without a physical presence.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to anchor substantial activities here, with the aim of creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That must be the objective of our economic policy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that means we will have to work even harder to attract and retain investments based on these non-tax competitive factors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Up to now EDB and our economic agencies have been very effective in bringing investments into Singapore and creating jobs for Singaporeans, but we should never take that for granted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We should never assume that these investments will just fall on our laps and they will automatically happen year after year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will get harder, so we will need all Singaporeans to support this critical mission; and that includes everyone in this House.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I am saying that with a reference to the upcoming debates on FTAs, because what we say, the tone of the debate does matter.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If investors start to feel that Singapore is starting to become less hospitable to foreign investments and talent, they will surely look for other options and there are many compelling options everywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And if not, is there room for further negotiations or seeking further carve-outs?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Or is it the case that Singapore, being a small country, will just be the price-taker?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is, the Minister mentioned about Pillar One, where the location of the taxing right will be given to countries where the customers are, I want to ask how significant is this reduction in the tax base and whether that will have any fiscal impact on our Budget.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there are still many design elements and implementation details that need to be worked out, as I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, how would the effective tax rate be determined?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are some technical details there to be resolved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Or whether there will be sectoral carve-outs, as I have mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For now, under Pillar Two, the one carve-out that is being proposed is for shipping.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because really, shipping operates under a very special tax regime.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It moves everywhere and to many different countries.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And so, you have different kinds of taxes for shipping, like tonnage tax, that falls outside of the scope of corporate taxes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Therefore, the intent or at least the proposal on the table now is to carve out shipping from Pillar Two.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They continue to be discussed at the Inclusive Forum.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore is an active participant in the forum and we will do our part to shape the consensus in line with our national interest and also to ensure a level playing field for everyone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this will have certainly a direct impact on our revenues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Exactly how much, like I said, it is difficult to give any detailed estimates now when the detailed rules are still being finalised.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And whether or not we will be able to make up with sufficient revenues elsewhere, that is something that we will have to work out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I should explain why we even ended up with Pillar One.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the reason is that many jurisdictions feel that in this new digital world, digitalisation has enabled large MNEs, especially the digital companies to do well, to grow dramatically and to be able to acquire more customers in jurisdictions outside of where they operate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And therefore, many of these market jurisdictions have started to unilaterally impose, what they call, digital services tax on these companies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not in our interest to have a taxation system that is fragmented and to have other jurisdictions impose unilateral taxes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is not helpful for Singapore as a small and open economy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why we feel it is better that we participate actively in the Inclusive Forum and be part of the multilateral discussion to shape a set of international tax rules that can be adapted to this new business model of the digital world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, indeed, that is what Pillar One is about.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As and when there is an agreement on Pillar One, the agreement will provide for the coordination of this new international proposal together with the removal of all digital services tax and other similar measures that have been unilaterally imposed by certain market jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have decided we could go along with this Pillar One consensus view, so that businesses can work with one set of rules rather than have to deal with a patchwork of fragmented rules.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as I mentioned, there are still details to be worked out even under Pillar One and these are issues which we will continue to actively discuss at the Inclusive Forum.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is, basically, in terms of the effective corporate income tax rates here in Singapore, what are they and whether the Government has conducted any scenario analysis to assess the net impact to our income tax revenues as a result of Pillars One and Two.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand that it is still preliminary days but we already have the key parameters.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: OECD, for example, has already given some sense of what it expects the global overall tax revenue impact is going to be.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second question is in terms of the foreign MNCs who are currently paying effective tax rates of below 15%, whether the Government would consider raising the effective tax rates to be in line with this minimum of 15%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And if I look at the US IRS data, for example, based on what has been disclosed, I think the effective tax rates for these US companies do appear to be much lower than our statutory income tax rates at just about 4%, and especially given that, as the Minister said, Singapore's attractiveness is not solely based on tax incentives alone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will provide the full answer there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yes, effectively, our effective corporate tax rate is low, not just for MNCs, but for all companies, especially for SMEs in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And they are low for a reason because we want to encourage business innovation, business investments and we want to make sure that businesses can create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, with Pillar Two being in place and with the consensus around Pillar Two forming at an effective rate of 15%, we will, of course, have to start thinking about what changes and adjustments are needed with regard to our corporate tax system to be in line with international standards, as I have said earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At this stage, I would just say it is premature to speculate or to talk about what these tax adjustments will be.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as I mentioned earlier, the key principle is we will preserve our sovereign tax rights, our rights to taxation, even within the international agreement, and we will work out together with businesses what adjustments and changes might be needed in our corporate tax system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is not something we should take lightly for the reasons I have explained earlier.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I specifically have a follow-on question with regard to tech companies in relation to what the Minister said about the digital economy.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Given both Pillars One and Two, and the impact of that – although I know that there are still a lot of uncertainties – how can Singapore, specifically, for the tech hub status, how can we continue to be attractive because both Pillars One and Two, could have significant impact on Singapore's tech hub status.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I would ask the Minister if he could elaborate on some of the key levers we would need to strengthen.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I know he talked about the whole breadth of it but what would be some of the key pillars for the tech sectors specifically, given the impact of digitalisation?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us be realistic about what the impact will be.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will make it harder for us to attract investments and we have to work harder, particularly, given our size, the fact that Singapore is such a small city-state, compared to so many other locations around the world which offer equally, if not more, attractive and compelling attributes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, whether it is for technology, whether it is for finance, whether, it is any other major investment that will now be impacted, we just have to work that much harder.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is what it comes down to, anywhere they go.
